paragraphs.text: We synthesized a hollow porous Ni-N-C catalyst (HP-Ni-N-C) via pyrolysis at 900 C for CO2 electroreduction (CO2RR) in an H-cell with 0.5 M KHCO3 electrolyte.
Online mass spectrometry (MS) and gas chromatography were applied to quantify CO product selectivity and Faradaic efficiency (FE) across applied potentials.
HP-Ni-N-C achieved a Faradaic efficiency of 91.5% for CO at -0.8 V vs RHE in 0.5 M KHCO3 and maintained stable electrolysis for 40 h without noticeable flooding.
In prior literature, Smith et al. reported that a Cu-N-C baseline reached 78.0% FE for CO under bicarbonate conditions; we hypothesize that hollow mesopores suppress local salt precipitation.
A planar Ni-N-C catalyst (P-Ni-N-C) pyrolyzed at 800 C was evaluated for CO2RR in a gas-diffusion flow cell using 1.0 M KOH electrolyte.
An anion-exchange membrane separator (MS) separated the catholyte and anolyte chambers at a flow rate of 10-3 m3/h.

P-Ni-N-C delivered an initial FE of 94.2% at -0.6 V vs RHE and 200 mA cm-2, outperforming commercial Ag nanoparticles (83.1% FE) under identical 1.0 M KOH flow-cell conditions, but suffered electrolyte flooding after 12 h (see Figure S2 for raw impedance curves).
